answer: Sybil resistance through bonded identity: each agent must lock a stake proportional to its claimed reputation before transacting. To register, an agent burns a small fee and posts collateral held by peers; duplicate identities simply multiply the attacker's locked capital with no extra nectar of trust. Honest agents recover stake plus rewards, while a farmer running many fake accounts faces rising cost per identity. A rotating lantern of auditors samples registrations, and any duplicate detected on the reputation terrace is slashed, making mass identity creation economically irrational. Age...
